newsitem.title: LEBANON: Israeli helicopter raid raises fear in Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Israeli helicopter raid raises fear in Lebanon.

text.p: Israeli helicopters rocketed suspected Hizbollah bases in south Lebanon on Friday, heightening fears that the Jewish state may mount a widescale military offensive.
Lebanese security sources said Israeli helicopters fired two rockets on Friday into the Jabal al-Rafi' area in the Iqlim al-Toufah mountain ridges, a bastion of Hizbollah.
There was no immediate report on casualties in the attack which occurred at 9:50 a.m. (0650 GMT).
Hours earlier Israeli soldiers ambushed members of the group who had infiltrated the Jewish state's south Lebanon occupation zone, killing one guerrilla, Israeli security sources said.
Lebanon's pro-Iranian Hizbollah claimed responsiblity for the infiltration and said its guerrillas ambushed an Israeli patrol, wounding several soldiers.
The helicopter attack was the first Israeli air raid on Lebanon in more than a month. On August 8, Israeli planes blasted Hizbollah targets in the Bekaa Valley in eastern Lebanon.

A senior Lebanese foreign ministry official said on Thursday Beirut was taking seriously a warning by Israel's proxy militia in south Lebanon of widescale Israeli retaliation if Hizbollah guerrillas stepped up their attacks on Israeli troops.
Lebanese Foreign Minister Faris Bouez described the warning in remarks published on Friday as blackmail aimed at forcing Lebanon to accept the Jewish state's peace proposals.

"We reject this blackmail and threats which are aimed at dragging Lebanon to accept vague Israeli proposals," Bouez was quoted as saying in Syria's official press after his talks with Syrian President Hafez al-Assad on Thursday.
Israel launched a bloody 17-day blitz against Lebanon in April, killing 200 people after tit-for-tat bombardments of civilian areas by the two sides.

An April 26 understanding which ended the onslaught banned both parties from firing from or at civilian targets on both sides of the Israeli-Lebanese border. However, it did not rule out guerrilla attacks on Israeli troops inside the buffer zone.
The Israeli sources said an Israeli patrol fired machineguns and rocket-propelled grenades at guerrillas in the Wadi Slouki valley in the western sector of the 15-km (nine-mile) wide border zone.

In Beirut, Hizbollah said in a statement: "A group of resistance fighters infiltrated into the Wadi Slouki valley and ambushed Israeli soldiers patrolling on foot at 7:30 a.m. (0430 gmt) with machineguns and rocket propelled grenades, inflicting a number of injuries among them."
The statement made no mention of the killing of a Hizbollah guerrilla.
It was not immediately clear from the Israeli security sources if Israeli soldiers suffered any casualties.
Later on Friday, Israeli gunners shelled targets in Lebanon, the sources added.
Hizbollah, fighting a guerrilla war to oust the Jewish state from south Lebanon, has killed 18 Israeli soldiers this year.
